angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 180,186 km at 31.48 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 31.7665 +/- 0.0142 mas (same row, RUWE 1.20): 31.48 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.259 +/- 0.013 solar radii from Barkaoui et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-6086 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...687A.264B/abstract): 180,186 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.254 +/- 0.013 solar masses from Barkaoui et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-6086 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...687A.264B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3200 +/- 75 K from Barkaoui et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6086 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...687A.264B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barkaoui et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6086 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...687A.264B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-6086.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.016, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
